name: Naproxen
executiveSummary: Long half-life NSAID. Adult: **250–500 mg PO every 12 h** (usual max **1 g/day**). Pediatrics ≥2 years: **5–10 mg/kg/day** divided q12h (max **1 g/day**).
indications:
## Indications

- Inflammatory pain, dysmenorrhea, arthritis, sprains; migraine (regimens).

## Precautions

- Same GI/renal/CV risks as other NSAIDs. Avoid in 3rd trimester.
- Base vs sodium: different mg equivalences — read the label.

adulto.dose: **250–500 mg PO every 12 h**. Acute/dysmenorrhea: often **500 mg** load then **250 mg q6–8h** or **500 mg q12h**. Usual max **1–1.25 g/day**.

pediatrico.dose: **5–10 mg/kg/day PO** divided every 12 h (max **15 mg/kg/day** or **1 g/day**).

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Dyspepsia, GI bleed, headache, edema, ↑ creatinine, rash.
